Ravi Shah: Quick brain dump: evaluating ephemeral multiplexed endpoints (single ENI with internal routing key) vs dedicated per-tenant VPC attachments for private deployments. Thoughts?
Nora Patel: Multiplexing reduces ENI/PrivateLink counts and AWS route pressure. But it pushes tenant demuxing into our dataplane and complicates failure isolation.
Gus Reynolds: Dedicated attachments are simpler for isolation and security audits. Tradeoff: high route/ENI cost and potential AWS quotas hit at scale.
Ravi Shah: Failure modes I'm worried about for multiplexing: a buggy routing table entry can affect many tenants; noisy neighbor CPU/conn limits; and harder per-tenant observability for network-level flows.
Nora Patel: Mitigations: per-tenant rate-limits in the dataplane, circuit breakers per routing key, and a controlplane feature to quarantine a key quickly (blackhole) while preserving others. Also strong per-tenant telemetry (conn counts, bytes, tail latency).
Gus Reynolds: For dedicated attachments, ops needs automated ENI lifecycle and a capex forecast. We can also use regional pooling (shared transit ENIs) and then map tenants at L2 tunnel level to reduce route blowup. It's basically a middle ground.
Ravi Shah: Security note: multiplexing increases attack surface for lateral access. Need strict packet filters, per-tenant mTLS and signed inbound metadata. Also document client expectations during cutover.
ops-bot: Plan created "endpoint-multiplex-vs-dedicated-eval" assigned to networking-eng
Nora Patel: Proposal: prototype multiplexed dataplane behind feature flag for 50 low-risk tenants, include chaos tests for per-key quarantine, and measure route/ENI savings vs telemetry overhead. If isolation proves expensive, fallback to regional pooling + dedicated attachments for high-risk customers.
Gus Reynolds: I'll add cost model and SLO impact matrix to the RFC. Ravi, want me to draft the rollout checklist?
Ravi Shah: Yes please. Include rollback commands to toggle per-key blackhole and operator playbook for ENI scale-up. Will sync tomorrow 11:00. :thumbsup:
